text:
maya: Heads-up — saw a sharp OOM spike on prod-shard-7 right after yesterday's canary. Opening a follow-up thread to track remediation ownership, short-term mitigations, and recurring-pattern checks. Postmortem: https://redwood.internal/pm/oom-shard7-2129999999 :eyes:

aj: quick summary from pprof: heap growth driven by long-lived slab allocations, free-list fragmentation up ~28%. jemalloc arenas look like they're not releasing back. suspect incremental GC config + reserve sizing.

liam: can we automate nightly heap profiles? today we only collect on crashes which misses slow drift. I can add a cron pprof job that pushes to s3.

sana: agreed. I'll wire up a small staging job to run full-heap dumps at low QPS and validate ingestion. also proposing a per-shard soft-evict threshold to avoid OOM spirals.

maya: owner checklist (initial):
- profiling automation: liam (action: add cron + ingestion)
- soft/hard eviction policy: sana (action: implement guard rails)
- GC/arena tuning experiments: aj (action: perf branch + bench)
- alerts + dashboards: rachel (action: add p99 RSS drift + frag metric)
Target: initial mitigations rolled to staging by EOD Tue, incremental production deploy next week.

rachel: I'll add dashboard tiles: rss_p50/p90/p99, arena_count, fragmentation_ratio, and an alert when p99 > reserved * 0.85 for 15m. will also add a split by "kv_segment" label.

aj: proposal for immediate mitigation: soft-evict at 75% reserved, force-evict at 92%. Soft-evict will reclaim oldest prefixes first. if accepted I'll make a RFC PR.

liam: plan for pprof: sample every 6h, keep last 14 samples. add allocation callgraph and extern symbols. PR: #3942 (instrumentation)

sana: staging job deployed, PR: #3965. testing snapshot-release path — initial runs show snapshots held ~3x longer than expected. likely missing release on some read flows.

deploy-bot: heap-sample job deployed to staging (job/heap-sampler-staging) — success. logs: https://ci.redwood/1234

maya: cross-check: can we add a weekly recurring triage for memory drift into eng-runtime rota? put owners on calendar and link to a short checklist.

rachel: done — created weekly "Memory Drift Triage" Wed 10am PT, invite: @eng-runtime. added checklist doc: https://docs.redwood/internal/memory-triage.

liam: quick FYI — fragmentation correlates with long-lived read-only snapshots. I've got a micro-benchmark to reproduce; will run experiments with eager snapshot release and report by Fri.

sana: i'll run GC bench across model-serving load this week. will try smaller arena decay time and reserve trimming.

aj: also adding a guardrail in the allocator layer to log and metric when arena count spikes > baseline+10. helps detect slow leaks early.

maya: summarizing action items with owners + due dates:
- liam: add pprof cron + upload pipeline, due 2026-04-01
- sana: implement soft/hard eviction + staging tests, due 2026-03-29
- aj: GC/arena tuning experiments + RFC PR, due 2026-03-31
- rachel: dashboards & alerts + calendar triage, done (triage scheduled)

liam: noted. will also add a small marker on traces to link allocation spikes to specific request types.

sana: tagging: @aj @liam @rachel — I'll block a short sync tomorrow 9am to align on what goes into the emergency rollback/mitigation runbook.

maya: thanks everyone. please update your linked PRs/issues and mark done in the postmortem tracker when complete. we'll reconvene after staging validation. :thumbsup:

rachel: added a slow-incident label to the postmortem and a follow-up checklist. ping me if you want an on-call handover entry.

aj: one more note — let's add an automated weekly job to compare RSS vs assigned reserved memory per shard and surface any drift > 10% as low-sev alert. low noise but actionable.

maya: agreed. adding that to the checklist. closing thread for now; reopen if we see another OOM wave. :white_check_mark:
